title: mRNA Synthesis and Encapsulation in Ionizable Lipid Nanoparticles
protocol: Mix reagents for the in vitro transcription (IVT) reaction.
Incubate the IVT reaction mixture at 37°C for the appropriate time period.
Combine vaccinia capping system and cap 2′-O-methyltransferase to enzymatically cap the mRNA transcript.
Incubate the capping reaction at 37°C for the specified duration.
Add Escherichia coli poly(A) polymerase to enzymatically tail the capped mRNA.
Incubate the tailing reaction at 37°C for the designated time period.
Mix reagents thoroughly before each incubation step.
Purify the mRNA away from DNA, salts, free nucleotides, and proteins using lithium chloride precipitation.
Clean the laminar flow hood or lab bench space to remove dust and RNase contamination.
Wipe down surfaces with 10% bleach, followed by RNase-free water or an RNase-decontaminant solution.
Wipe pipettes and tip boxes with RNase-decontaminant solution.
Wear clean gloves at all times that have been sterilized with RNase-decontaminant solution.
Remove a single tube of each reagent required for IVT from the freezer and transfer to the clean laminar flow hood or lab bench.
Allow the 10× T7 reaction buffer and NTPs to equilibrate to room temperature.
Mix NTPs equally into a 100 mM final concentration.
Spin the mixture in a mini-centrifuge for 10 seconds at maximum speed at room temperature.
Use micropipettes to combine NTPs for future reactions.
Add required amounts of reagents listed in Table 1 to reach a total volume of 16 µl.
Mix the reaction thoroughly by vortexing.
Spin the reaction mixture in a mini-centrifuge for 10 seconds at maximum speed at room temperature.
Add DNA template and RNA polymerase as listed in Table 2 to reach a final volume of 20 µl.
Gently mix with a pipette.
Spin the tube in a mini-centrifuge for 10 seconds at maximum speed at room temperature.
Incubate tubes in a thermocycler or heat block for 2 hr once 37°C is reached.
Thaw the tube of DNase I buffer.
Mix the DNase I buffer after thawing.
Add reagents to the reaction in the order listed in Table 3.
Mix the reaction gently with a pipette.
Incubate the reaction for 15 min at 37°C in the heat block or thermocycler.
Store DNase I buffer in 10 µl aliquots if reactions will be carried out frequently.
Transfer the DNase I-treated IVT reaction to an appropriate tube for centrifugation.
Add half the sample volume of 6 M lithium chloride to the reaction.
If precipitating a small amount of mRNA, add glycogen at 1 µg/µl together with the lithium chloride.
Mix the reaction and lithium chloride mixture by gently inverting the tube.
Spin the mixture in a mini-centrifuge for 10 seconds at maximum speed, room temperature.
Store the sample at −20°C for at least 30 minutes.
Cool the centrifuge to 4°C.
Spin the sample for at least 30 minutes at >14,000 × g, 4°C.
Discard the lithium chloride and retain the pellet.
Wash the sample by adding 1 ml pre-chilled 70% ethanol.
Gently flick the tube until the pellet comes loose in the ethanol.
Spin the pellet down for 5 minutes at >14,000 × g, 4°C.
Discard the ethanol and retain the pellet.
Remove as much ethanol as possible with a pipette.
Allow the pellet to dry.
Mix 15 mM sterile HCl with human recombinant leptin.
Resuspend the mRNA pellet in 150 µl nuclease-free water by pipetting gently up and down.
Incubate the resuspended mRNA pellet at 4°C for ≥15 min before pipetting if time allows.
Take an aliquot of at least 5 μl of mRNA for quality control.
Measure and record the concentration of the mRNA using a nanodrop spectrophotometer by measuring absorbance at 260 nm.
Store the sample at 4°C if quality control will be carried out on the same day.
Freeze the sample short-term at -20°C or long-term at -80°C if quality control will be carried out more than 24 hours later.
Dilute mRNA 1:5 in nuclease-free water if the concentration is likely to be outside of the absorbance limits of the instrument.
Measure the concentration of diluted mRNA on the nanodrop at 260 nm.
Calculate A260/280 and A260/230 ratios as indicators for purity.
Heat one heat block or thermocycler, water bath, or incubator to 65°C.
Heat another heat block or thermocycler, water bath, or incubator to 37°C.
Remove a single tube of 10× capping buffer, GTP, and SAM from the freezer and allow it to equilibrate to room temperature.
Mix the removed tube thoroughly in a mini-centrifuge at maximum speed for 10 seconds.
Denature the precipitated mRNA from the IVT reaction at 65°C for 5 min.
Immediately cool the denatured mRNA in a cold block for approximately 5 min.
Add all reagents listed in Table 4 to an Eppendorf tube in the specified order.
Mix the added reagents thoroughly.
Spin the mixture in a mini-centrifuge for 10 seconds at maximum speed.
Cap 150 µg of mRNA in a 300 µl reaction.
Adjust the values in Table 4 to match the amount of input mRNA from the previous step.
Optionally add RNase inhibitor at temperatures below 50°C after the denaturation step.
Add the denatured and cooled mRNA to the reaction.
Gently pipette to mix enzymes with the reaction as listed in Table 5.
Spin the tube in a mini-centrifuge for 10 seconds at maximum speed, room temperature.
Incubate the reaction at 37°C for 1 hour.
Incubate the cap-2′-O-methyltransferase with mRNA according to specified conditions.
Precipitate the mRNA as described in steps 8 to 14.
Take an aliquot of at least 5 μl of the capped mRNA for quality control.
Measure and record the concentration of the mRNA using a nanodrop spectrophotometer.
Heat the heat block, thermocycler, or water bath to 37°C.
Add reagents in Table 6 to set up the enzymatic tailing reaction in the order listed.
Mix gently after adding the reagents.
Spin the mixture in a mini-centrifuge for 10 seconds at maximum speed.
Incubate the mixture at 37°C for 1 hour.
Incubate the capped mRNA at an appropriate temperature and time for tailing reaction.
Proceed directly to precipitate the capped and tailed mRNA as described in steps 8 to 13.
Resuspend the washed pellet in slightly less nuclease-free water than above aiming for a concentration above 1 mg/ml.
Resuspend the pellet in nuclease-free water.
Take an aliquot of at least 5 μl of the capped and tailed mRNA for quality control.
Measure and record the concentration of the mRNA using a nanodrop spectrophotometer.
Adjust the mRNA to a final concentration of 1 mg/ml in 100 mM sodium acetate buffer, pH 3 to 5.
Calculate the volume of nuclease-free water (VWater) needed for adjustment.
Calculate the volume of 3 M sodium acetate (VNaOAc) needed for adjustment.
Aliquot the mRNA into 100 µl single-use aliquots.
Freeze the aliquoted mRNA at -80°C for long-term storage.
Measure agarose and add to appropriate volume of 1× TAE buffer to make a 1% gel.
Mix agarose and buffer, then melt in microwave.
Add 1 µl SYBR Safe (10,000× stock) for every 10 ml of melted mixture.
Pour the mixed solution into a gel tray with comb to set.
Run samples from post-IVT, post-capping, and post-tailing on the agarose gel adjacently.
Prepare the ssRNA ladder by adding 3 µl ladder to 9 µl 2× RNA loading dye.
Denature the ladder for 5 min at 72°C in a pre-heated heat block, thermocycler, or PCR thermocycler programmed to reach 72°C.
Prepare samples by adding 2× RNA loading dye and mRNA samples 1:1.
Denature the samples for 5 min at 72°C in a pre-heated heat block, thermocycler, or PCR thermocycler programmed to reach 72°C.
Submerge gel in running cell filled with 1× TAE buffer.
Remove comb and load ssRNA ladder followed by samples.
Include a control sample of mRNA from the IVT reaction as a reference to screen for size increase.
Run gel at 120 V for 45 min.
Image gel and assess the presence of the poly(A) tail after enzymatic tailing reaction through an increase in size on the gel.
Dilute samples to approximately 100 ng/μl in nuclease-free water.
Remove a 1 μl aliquot of RNA ScreenTape ladder from the −80°C freezer and place it on ice.
Pipette 5 μl sample buffer into each tube that will contain a sample plus one extra tube for the ladder.
Pipette 1 μl of each sample into a tube containing sample buffer.
Cover the tubes using optical caps.
Mix the samples by shaking the tubes in an orbital shaker at 2000 rpm for approximately 1 minute.
Spin the tubes in a mini-centrifuge at maximum speed for 10 seconds at room temperature.
Heat the samples in a PCR thermocycler for 3 minutes at 72°C.
Cool the tubes immediately on ice for 2 minutes.
Centrifuge the samples in a mini-centrifuge for 10 seconds at maximum speed, room temperature.
Place all liquid at the bottom of the tubes before proceeding.
Insert the labeled samples into the TapeStation 4150 machine after removing the caps.
Load an RNA ScreenTape into the TapeStation and label the samples using the controller software.
Click start to begin the run, following all prompts.
View results in the TapeStation analysis software.
Delete all peaks (18S and 28S) from the sample peak view.
Reassign a sample peak by right clicking > add peak.
Press the region button to define the peak region of the mRNA.
Add an upper and lower size value to the defined region.
Observe the percentage of mRNA within the defined region from the region table.
Define the region based on user-defined criteria or peak position (e.g., ±1000 bases from the peak).
Use a region spanning 1000 nt either side of the detected peak for analysis.
Work in an environment that is nuclease-free to prevent degradation of the mRNA.
Ensure a sterile environment if particles are to be used in biological experiments.
Use sterile reagents and consumables for biological experiments.
Mix Dlin-MC3-DMA, cholesterol, DSPC, and DMG-PEG2000 as required.
Dilute mRNA in aqueous solution at 1 mg/ml in sodium acetate buffer pH 5.
Store diluted mRNA at -80°C until use.
Allow lipids to equilibrate to room temperature before opening.
Weigh at least 3 mg of each lipid individually using a 4 decimal place balance.
Weigh the ionizable lipid using an autopipette and transfer it to a vial.
Ensure the lipid is weighed rather than measured by volume due to viscosity.
Aliquot MC3 lipid at 10 to 15 mg into small amber vials.
Store aliquots of MC3 in an airtight container with desiccant at -20°C.
Add ethanol to lipids using an autopipette to achieve a final concentration of 10 mg/ml.
Warm cholesterol, DSPC, and DMG-PEG2000 if needed by holding the vial under warm running water.
Dissolve any white solids in the lipid solution until it becomes clear.
Remove precipitates that may form upon storage at -20°C by warming as described.
Prepare the lipid mixture solution as described in the protocol.
Vortex briefly to mix the lipid mixture.
Store the lipids mixture at -20°C for later use.
Wipe down the laminar flow hood with 70% ethanol.
Clean pipettes with 70% ethanol.
Spray gloves with RNase-decontaminant solution before use.
Spray vials of lipids with RNase-decontaminant solution before opening.
Prepare two Amicon Ultra-15 centrifugal concentrators.
Add 10 ml DPBS and centrifuge for 20 minutes at 4000 × g, room temperature.
Discard filtrate and retentate.
Add 13 ml DPBS to each tube immediately after discarding the previous contents.
Do not allow spin filters to dry out once wet.
Thaw 300 µg of mRNA aliquot(s) in the fridge (4°C) or on ice.
Allow thawed mRNA to warm to room temperature just before use.
Prepare 100 mM pH 5 sodium acetate buffer by diluting 1 ml of 3 M stock into 30 ml with RNase-free, sterile water.
Dilute the mRNA aliquot with room temperature 100 mM sodium acetate buffer to adjust its concentration to 241.5 µg/ml.
Combine multiple mRNA aliquots into one Eppendorf tube if necessary.
Adjust the volume of the combined mRNA solution by adding appropriate buffer to reach a total volume suitable for formulation, such as 1.6 ml.
Enter the formulation parameters into the NanoAssemblr Ignite according to specified settings.
Set the total volume parameter in NanoAssemblr Ignite to reflect the scale of formulation desired, typically at least 0.4 ml.
Insert a new NxGen cartridge into the instrument and check that it has been recognized.
Insert the waste and 15-ml sample centrifuge tubes.
Draw the aqueous mRNA solution into the 3-ml syringe using a blunt needle.
Invert the syringe to tap out any air bubbles and remove the needle.
Plunge the syringe to remove remaining air, then place it firmly in the C position of the cartridge.
Draw the lipids solution into the 1-ml syringe using a blunt needle.
Remove the needle and plunge the syringe so that there is no air remaining.
Place the syringe firmly in the R position of the cartridge.
Ensure the instrument is in the ready state and start the formulation.
Ensure the volume in each syringe is at least a syringe-graduation more than displayed on the instrument.
Transfer the lipid nanoparticle suspension to DPBS in pre-rinsed spin filters immediately after formulation.
Split the formulation evenly between two spin filters, for example 0.65 ml to each filter.
Concentrate the iLNP solution by centrifugation at ≤4000 × g for 30 min at 4°C.
Repeat the centrifugation step if necessary until the volume is reduced to the initial amount added, such as 0.65 ml.
Transfer the concentrated iLNP solution to a sterile, RNase-free vessel and note the final volume.
Pipette up and down several times to ensure iLNP is suspended in the spin filter.
Remove solution from the filter.
Characterize the iLNP as desired according to Basic Protocol 3.
Perform the RiboGreen assay to determine encapsulation efficiency and concentration of encapsulated mRNA.
Use DPBS to adjust the concentration of the solution to 100 µg/ml if necessary.
Store the iLNP solution at 4°C.
Characterize the iLNP before use if stored for more than 1 month.
Generate lipid nanoparticles using microfluidics.
Complex mRNA to cationic iLNP at low pH.
Fusion of lipid nanoparticles occurs at neutral pH.
Concentrate the complexed mixture.
Analyze the final product.
Thaw at least 150 µg of the mRNA aliquot(s) in the fridge (4°C) or on ice.
Allow thawed mRNA to warm to room temperature just before use.
Adjust buffer to 1 mg/ml with 3 M acetate stock solution if necessary.
Insert a new NxGen cartridge into the instrument and check that it has been recognized.
Draw more than the required volume of 100 mM acetate buffer into the 3-ml syringe using a blunt needle.
Invert the syringe to dislodge any air bubbles and tap the syringe.
Remove the needle and plunge the syringe to remove remaining air.
Place the syringe firmly in the C position of the cartridge.
Draw the lipids solution into the 1-ml syringe using a blunt needle.
Remove the needle and plunge the syringe so that there is no air remaining.
Place the syringe firmly in the R position of the cartridge.
Ensure the instrument is in the ready state and start the formulation.
Add at least 1.25 ml to the aqueous syringe before formulation begins.
Ensure the volume in each syringe is at least a syringe graduation more than displayed on the instrument.
When the formulation of preformed vesicles is complete, immediately add the appropriate volume of preformed vesicle to the mRNA solution and pipette up and down to mix thoroughly.
Transfer the lipid nanoparticle suspension to DPBS in pre-rinsed spin filters evenly between two filters.
Dilute the iLNP solution 15-30 times in DPBS.
Follow steps 15-18 of Basic Protocol 2.
Conduct routine analysis and quality control of iLNPs as described in Basic Protocol 3.
Determine mRNA concentration and encapsulation efficiency using RiboGreen.
Measure particle size and zeta potential using DLS.
Extract mRNA from nanoparticles to assess integrity.
Perform an assay to determine the apparent pKa of particles (optional).
Carry out the RiboGreen experiment first to determine encapsulation efficiency and concentration of encapsulated mRNA.
Adjust the mRNA concentration to 100 μg/ml according to Basic Protocol 2, step 17.
Conduct DLS analysis using the diluted solution.
Determine the apparent pKa using the diluted solution.
Extract mRNA from the diluted solution for further analysis.
Add Triton X-100 to the iLNP sample to disrupt particles for RiboGreen assay.
Measure particle size and polydispersity index using dynamic light scattering (DLS).
Measure zeta potential of particles using DLS instrument.
Measure the fluorescence of TNS in buffers with pH 3 to 9.
Determine the apparent pKa of particles by generating a pH titration curve for the iLNP using TNS fluorescence data.
Remove QuantIT RiboGreen RNA reagent kit from the fridge and warm to room temperature.
Prepare 1× TE buffer by diluting 1 ml of 20× TE stock solution in 19 ml RNase-free water.
Add 400 μl Triton X-100 to the diluted 1× TE buffer to prepare a 2% Triton buffer.
Pour the prepared buffers into separate pipette basins if using a multichannel pipette.
In the top row (A) of a 96-well plate, add 7.5 μl of each iLNP solution and a DPBS blank.
Add 1× TE buffer to each well to achieve a final volume of 250 μl.
Pipette up and down to mix the contents in each well.
Add 242.5 μl of 1× TE buffer to a 7.5 μl aliquot.
Add 50 μl of 1× TE buffer to the two wells below the samples (rows B and C).
Add 50 μl of 2% Triton buffer to the two wells below the samples (rows D and E).
Depress the pipette knob to the second stop to aspirate liquid and to the first stop to express liquid, with liquid remaining in the tip.
Add 50 μl of diluted sample from row A to each of the four wells below (rows B, C, D, and E).
Dilute RNA standard or mRNA from the formulation to 20 µg/ml with 1× TE buffer.
Set up a standard curve in duplicate according to Table 12.
Incubate the plate at 37°C for 10 min.
Dilute RiboGreen dye reagent 1:100 in 1×TE buffer.
Vortex the diluted RiboGreen solution to mix thoroughly.
Calculate the volume of RiboGreen dye required based on the number of samples and standards.
Add 26 μl of RiboGreen dye reagent to 2.6 ml of 1× TE buffer for a final volume of 2.626 ml.
Add 100 µl of diluted RiboGreen solution to each sample and standard well.
Pop any bubbles in the wells with a needle if present.
Read fluorescence using λex 485 nm and λem 528 nm on a plate reader.
Plot the standard curve using data from the fluorescence readings.
Calculate the concentration of mRNA in the sample wells based on the standard curve.
Determine the concentration of mRNA in the bulk solution according to Equation 4.
Subtract the concentration of samples without Triton X-100 from the samples with Triton X-100.
Average duplicate sample concentrations.
Use this value and known volume to dilute the sample to 100 µg/ml encapsulated mRNA.
Divide the concentration of encapsulated mRNA by the concentration of the well with Triton X-100 (total mRNA) and multiply by 100.
Turn on the DLS instrument at least 30 minutes prior to use.
Set the temperature of the instrument to 25°C.
Dilute 10 µl of the 100 µg/ml iLNP sample with 90 µl DPBS in a disposable low volume zetasizer cuvette.
Insert the cuvette into the instrument and collect DLS data.
Average the results of the three acquisitions in the DLS software.
Report the z-average as the particle size and polydispersity index.
Dilute 20 μl of the 100 μg/ml iLNP solution with 980 μl water in an Eppendorf tube.
Flush the zeta potential cuvette with ethanol by taking up 1-2 ml ethanol in a 3-ml syringe and flushing through the capillary into an empty syringe, then flush back. Repeat 2 to 3 times.
Repeat the flushing process with water.
Remove all liquid from the cuvette ensuring it is dry inside.
Load the diluted iLNP sample into one port of the zeta potential cuvette using a fresh syringe.
Invert the cuvette and inject the sample until it fills about half of the U tube.
Carefully return the cuvette to an upright position and continue injecting the rest of the sample to just below the ‘fill’ line.
Ensure there are no air bubbles in the sample before removing the syringe and fitting stoppers.
Insert the prepared zeta potential cuvette into the instrument for data collection.
Set dispersant as water with a refractive index of 1.330, viscosity of 0.8872 cP, dielectric constant of 78.5, and temperature at 25°C.
Allow equilibration time of 120 seconds before starting the measurement.
Collect zeta potential data for three measurements as determined by the instrument based on count rate.
Determine the measurement duration and attenuator setting based on the sample using the DLS software.
Average the results of three acquisitions in the DLS software and report the zeta potential in millivolts (mV).
Remove the sample from the instrument by attaching a syringe to one port and drawing up the solution until half of the U-bend is empty.
Invert the cell and remove the remaining contents with a syringe attached to one port.
Repeat the wash step with water as described previously.
Flush the cuvette with ethanol if it will not be used for another sample, then leave to dry.
Prepare RNA wash buffer by diluting the RNA wash buffer concentrate five-fold with ethanol.
In an RNase-free Eppendorf tube add 20 μl of the iLNP sample at 100 µg/ml, followed by 10 μl RNA lysis buffer and 10 μl ethanol.
Pipette up and down to mix.
Transfer the solution to a Zymo-Spin IC column in a collection tube.
Centrifuge for 30 seconds at 10,000 to 16,000 × g at room temperature.
Discard the flow through.
Add 400 µl of RNA prep buffer to the column.
Centrifuge as in step 32.
Discard the flow through.
Add 700 µl of RNA wash buffer to the column.
Centrifuge as in step 32.
Discard the flow through.
Add 400 µl of RNA wash buffer to the column.
Centrifuge for 60 seconds at 10,000 to 16,000 × g at room temperature.
Transfer the column to a new RNase-free Eppendorf tube.
Add 15 µl of RNase-free water to the column.
Centrifuge as in step 32.
Analyze the extracted mRNA by automated gel electrophoresis as per Basic Protocol 1 steps 34 to 41.
Alternatively, analyze the extracted mRNA by 1% agarose gel electrophoresis following Basic Protocol 1 steps 30 to 33.
Portion phosphate-citrate-borate buffer evenly across 20 containers (50 ml each).
Adjust the pH of each aliquot using 1 M NaOH and 1 M HCl to achieve increments between pH 3 and 9 (∼0.3 units).
Stir contents in Nalgene bottles with a magnetic flea.
Vortex centrifuge tubes before measurement.
Ensure solution is properly mixed prior to taking a pH measurement.
Estimate pH using a digital pH meter followed by precise measurement with a benchtop pH meter with multipoint calibration.
Store pH-adjusted stocks frozen for later use; re-measure pH after freeze-thaw cycles.
Ensure thawed buffer has reached room temperature before use in the assay or measuring the pH.
Dissolve TNS reagent in DMSO to 1 mg/ml by dissolving 1 mg of TNS reagent in 1 ml DMSO.
Take 100 µl of the 1 mg/ml stock solution and add 900 µl DMSO to make a 0.1 mg/ml solution.
Store both solutions frozen (-20°C) in the dark for later use.
Aliquot 1 ml of each buffer into an appropriate container such as an Eppendorf tube or cryovial.
Add 22 µl of 0.1 mg/ml TNS in DMSO solution to each buffer and vortex.
Discard solutions when done with the assay; do not freeze for future use.
Add 2.5 μl of each iLNP sample into 20 wells of an opaque or black walled 96-well plate.
Layout samples according to the specified arrangement.
Add 92.5 μl of each buffer containing TNS into the wells with iLNP sample.
Read the fluorescence of the TNS reagent using λex 325 nm and λem 435 nm.
Convert the fluorescence readings to relative fluorescence by dividing all values by the highest reading.
Fit the relative fluorescence data to the Henderson-Hasselbalch equation.
Report the apparent pKa for each lipid (pH at which half of the maximum TNS fluorescence is reached).
